subject: NimbusHealth launch: temporary throttle exemption & traffic forecast
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, Jul 18, 2026 at 11:22 AM -0400
Subject: NimbusHealth launch: temporary throttle exemption & traffic forecast

Team —

Nimbus Health (early adopter, onboarding this week) just confirmed a phased public launch for their patient triage feature. They asked us for an elevated rate-limit window during their first 72 hours of public traffic so they don’t see 429s while they ramp. They will be on our hosted API (no Dedicated pool).

Quick context and ask: 
- Launch window: 2026-07-22 09:00 ET start (internal GA announcement) for ~72 hours.
- Forecast (attached): peak burst ~950 requests/sec at minute granularity, average request size ~1.1k tokens (prompt+expected completion). Expected sustained during core hours: 220-300 rps.
- Primary model: redwood/open-instruct-13b (we may toggle to smaller variant if needed).
- Customer expects <2s p50 latency; they will accept graceful degradation if we fall back to smaller model.

Primary asks: 
1) Can infra/product grant a temporary throttle exemption (or bump per-customer QPS) up to 1k rps for the 72h window, with a rolling cap if needed?
2) What mitigations do we need on our side (batching, prefix cache warmup, autoscale knobs) to keep latency reasonable?
3) Any documented risk or SLA implications we should surface to the customer?

Attachments: nimbus_launch_forecast_v2.csv (per-minute forecast) and nimbus_slo_notes.pdf (customer SLO ask).

I put Karthik in the thread to confirm product-level rollout policy and Marissa for capacity confirmation. Neha — can you confirm routing/model fallback plan?

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, Jul 19, 2026 at 09:40 AM -0400
Subject: Re: NimbusHealth launch: temporary throttle exemption & traffic forecast

Laura — thanks for the heads up and the forecast. A few clarifying questions before I sign off on an exception path: 

1) Can you confirm the per-minute peak from the CSV (I want the max-minute request count and the 95th percentile per-minute)? 950 rps as a 1-minute burst vs sustained will change the mitigation approach.
2) Will the customer accept a staged increase (e.g., 300 -> 600 -> 1k) based on observed health signals? If so, what are the exact health signals they accept for stepups?
3) Are they on any specific model pin (do they require the 13b) or can we default to open-instruct-6b for fallback?
4) Any requirement around tokenization differences (some of our quantized variants change tokenization slightly; want to surface to them).

Assuming we can stage and they accept fallback, product is comfortable with a temporary policy exception. I want infra to confirm we can autoscale quickly and whether we need a manual burst pool. Also cc’ing Legal briefly — if we do an exception that impacts other customers, we should log it for the SLA exceptions register.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Management | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, Jul 19, 2026 at 1:05 PM -0400
Subject: Re: NimbusHealth launch: temporary throttle exemption & traffic forecast

Laura / team — I pulled the forecast and ran it through capacity sims. Short answers first: yes, we can support a controlled bump, but there are constraints and one recommended path. Details below.

Capacity summary (hosted pool, us-east region):
- Current headroom on standard pool: ~350 rps sustained at p95 for the 13b workload before latencies exceed 2s.
- Cold-start risk on minute-scale bursts: if we get sustained 1-min bursts >700 rps we’ll see queueing and p95 will spike to ~4s without additional workers pinned.
- Recommended temporary plan: provision a 48-hour burst pool (reserved workers) that adds capacity equivalent to ~1.2k rps for redwood/open-instruct-13b; allow a staged throttle increase (300 -> 600 -> 1k) with automated rollback on error rate or latency thresholds.

Operational requirements and mitigations: 
- Warm-up: pre-load KV cache for top prefixes (we need the top 50 prompt prefixes from customer, ideally 24h before launch).
- Batching: increase request batch windows slightly during peak minutes (configurable per-route) — reduces GPU token cost and helps with throughput while maintaining p50 latency.
- Autoscale: auto-scale rules will be temporarily relaxed, but we still need manual ops oversight for the first 12 hours.
- Fallback models: we can route to open-instruct-6b for non-critical traffic; must confirm with the customer on quality tradeoffs.

Risk & SLA notes: 
- This is an exception to our default per-customer quotas; we will log the exception and time-box it.
- If other customers contend for the same pool, we may need redispatch rules — we propose using prioritization tags to protect the burst pool.

Timing and lead time: we can spin up the burst pool in 48 hours if we get an explicit approval by EOD Jul 20. I will need the signed exception form (DocuSign) and the prefix list.

Attachments: attached simulated latency curves (see Drive link).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, Jul 19, 2026 at 4:20 PM -0400
Subject: Re: NimbusHealth launch: temporary throttle exemption & traffic forecast

Marking a couple of product/routing items: 

- Model pinning: we can support route-level fallback to open-instruct-6b automatically after error-rate > 2% for 2 consecutive minutes. That will keep tokens flowing while preserving the 13b for high-value requests. We need explicit approval from the customer for any model downgrade that may change output.
- Prefix cache: Laura — if Nimbus can share the top 50 most common prompts by Monday morning (Jul 20 09:00 ET) we’ll pre-warm. If they can only share examples and not exact PII, that’s fine — we just need representative prefixes.
- Rate-limit config: I’ll prepare a per-route config that stages the QPS and toggles fallback. Marissa — can you confirm the route id I should use to target the burst pool?

Also note for the team: please ensure the security/compliance docket (SOC2 evidence) is ready if Nimbus requests it during launch; they previously asked for audit-log access for the pilot.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Product Engineer, Serving | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Verma <amit@nimbushealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, Jul 20, 2026 at 12:15 PM -0400
Subject: Re: NimbusHealth launch: temporary throttle exemption & traffic forecast

Thanks all — this is great and aligned. Quick summary / mutual action plan so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Customer: Nimbus Health
   - Confirmed launch start: 2026-07-22 09:00 ET, 72-hour window.
   - They will provide top 50 prompt prefixes by Mon Jul 20 09:00 ET (Amit is copied).
   - They accept staged increase and fallback to 6b for non-core requests.

2) Infra (Marissa): provision 48-hour burst pool sized to support up to 1.2k rps for 13b; staged QPS ramp (300 -> 600 -> 1k). Manual ops oversight first 12 hours. Approval needed by EOD Jul 20 to meet 48h lead time.

3) Product (Karthik/Neha): prepare route config with staged throttle and automatic fallback to open-instruct-6b on latency/error triggers. Neha to confirm route id and pre-warm plan.

4) Sales/CS: Laura to send exception DocuSign and customer comms confirming we’re timeboxing to 72 hours.

5) Legal/Tracking: Karthik to log the SLA exception ticket; Rishi to file for visibility.

Next steps:
- I will send the DocuSign link to Amit today and ask for explicit sign-off.
- Marissa — please confirm once the burst pool is provisioned (or if you need additional approvals).
- Neha — please post the route id and the fallback thresholds in this thread.

Amit — appreciate quick turn here. We’ll keep your ingress prioritized and monitor token usage closely.

Laura
